candidates.name: Behcet's disease
support_spans: intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations
genital and oral ulcers were also present
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of recurrent oral and genital ulcers, along with skin lesions, are consistent with Behcet's disease.

candidates.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
support_spans: painful leg ulcers
violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and a fibrinous base
candidates.why: The patient's leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders, eschar, and a fibrinous base are characteristic of Pyoderma gangrenosum.

candidates.name: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
support_spans: Monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
Phenotypically abnormal T-cell population with CD52 expression
candidates.why: The patient's skin biopsies showing atypical lymphocytic infiltrate and abnormal T-cell population suggest a diagnosis of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

candidates.name: Wegener's granulomatosis
support_spans: elevated C-reactive protein, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
spleno-megaly and involvement of retroperitoneal, pelvic, and inguinal lymph nodes
candidates.why: The patient's laboratory findings and systemic imaging results are consistent with a diagnosis of Wegener's granulomatosis.

candidates.name: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
support_spans: Skin biopsy (left thigh): Monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
Immunohistochemical staining: CD3-positive T cells coexpressing CD4 and CD8 with preserved expression of CD7
candidates.why: The patient's skin biopsy and immunohistochemical staining results are decisive for a diagnosis of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

candidates.name: Polyarteritis nodosa
support_spans: Doppler ultrasound of lower extremities showed venous stasis
Systemic imaging revealed splenomegaly and involvement of retroperitoneal, pelvic, and inguinal lymph nodes
candidates.why: The patient's imaging results are consistent with a diagnosis of Polyarteritis nodosa.
